run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: I searched app-254-prod-logs over the whole authorized window and got back every document it holds (12, timestamps 2026-11-22T04:28:09Z to 09:28:09Z). The logs show a production DR test (correlation_id dr-test-001) starting at 04:28:09Z that switched to a failover database, followed by Company.Ops errors that name that failover: a 30s connection timeout to the failover DB and 'unable to acquire database lock during failover' at 05:28:09Z (job-8827, status 500), the job-creation endpoint returning 503 'database failover in progress' at 06:28:09Z, and the job-creation failure the user described at 07:28:09Z: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' (correlation_id job-8831, host ops-prod-02). Company.Ops recovered in the logs only after 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (08:28:09Z) and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' (09:28:09Z). The exact name 'companyopswebjob' does not appear in the index, in any message, or as a Kubernetes object in the queried cluster: the only service identities in the index are Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, and the Kubernetes objects available are the opentelemetry-demo cluster, so the host-level Company.Ops application could not be inspected directly. Independent checks found no competing cause in the available cluster evidence: the only fault-injection ConfigMap (otel-demo/flagd-config) has every flag off, no Company.Ops-like deployment/pod/service exists, and the only in-window cluster events are two unrelated Endpoints warnings. A cluster-wide in-place container restart at 08:04:13Z was checked and is not tied to this fault (it is later than the errors and involves a different system). Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this run, and the change-history integration is not available, so DB-side metrics/traces and the DR-test change record could not be verified.

claims.text: app-254-prod-logs held 12 documents and the window query returned all 12 (total relation eq, documents_shown 12, all shards successful), spanning 2026-11-22T04:28:09Z to 2026-11-22T09:28:09Z; no document was omitted.
At 2026-11-22T04:28:09Z service Company.Ops on host ops-prod-01 logged INFO with correlation_id dr-test-001: 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database'.
At 2026-11-22T05:28:09Z Company.Ops (ops-prod-01, correlation_id dr-test-001) logged ERROR: 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'.
At 2026-11-22T05:28:09Z Company.Ops (ops-prod-01, correlation_id job-8827) logged ERROR: 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover'.

At 2026-11-22T06:28:09Z Company.Ops on host ops-prod-02 (correlation_id dr-test-001) logged WARN: 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' (a 503, distinct from the 500 entries).

At 2026-11-22T07:28:09Z Company.Ops on host ops-prod-02 (correlation_id job-8831) logged ERROR: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' — the only log line matching the reported failed new-scheduled-job creation with a 500.

Company.Ops logged INFO 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' at 2026-11-22T08:28:09Z and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' at 2026-11-22T09:28:09Z; no Company.Ops ERROR appears after 07:28:09Z in the 12 returned documents.

Service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob on radar-prod-01 logged its own ERRORs: 05:28:09Z 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover' and 06:28:09Z 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted', a WARN retry after backoff at 07:28:09Z, and INFO 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery' at 08:28:09Z.

The 12 documents contain only two service values — Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents); no document carries a service field or message text 'companyopswebjob', so nothing in the index matches that exact name.

The queried Kubernetes cluster (target m0-otel-20260909) contains 24 Deployments in namespaces kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo — all of them either cluster add-ons or opentelemetry-demo components (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, plus jaeger/prometheus/alertmanager/otel-collector/kube-state-metrics) — and none is named companyopswebjob or belongs to a Company.Ops application; every listed deployment shows its desired replica ready and available.

The only pods whose names matched compan/ops/webjob/radar are kube-system control-plane pods (etcd-, kube-apiserver-, kube-controller-manager-, kube-scheduler-opspilot-m1-control-plane), not an application webjob.

The only ConfigMap with fault/delay-injection settings is otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json): productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad each have defaultVariant 'off'; none refers to Company.Ops, a job scheduler or a database failover.

Across all namespaces, all 32 pods show a last container termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown; metrics-server, kube-state-metrics, local-path-provisioner, prometheus-readonly-proxy exited with codes 1/2 shortly after) and are Running and ready now with restart counts of 1–6; the etcd/kube-apiserver/kube-controller-manager/kube-scheduler control-plane containers restarted in place at 08:04:14Z with the same pod names.

Only two events exist in the window across all namespaces, both Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint for default-namespace services (app-219/mariadb 'endpoints "mariadb" already exists' at 10:07:47Z and app-162/signup-service at 09:32:52Z); neither involves Company.Ops, pods or nodes.

The production DR test dr-test-001 (switch to the failover database at 04:28:09Z) is the cause of the Company.Ops 500/503 failures: every Company.Ops error from 05:28:09Z to 07:28:09Z names the failover DB, the failover lock state, or the jobs table, and the error sequence ends only after 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (08:28:09Z). The deeper cause would then be in the failover database (connection timeout, lock not obtainable during failover, connection pool exhaustion, deadlock on the jobs table) rather than in Company.Ops itself.

The Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob errors are most likely a cascade of the Company.Ops/DB failover rather than an independent fault, but the only support is the radar logger's own text ('upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover'); no shared trace or DB signal is available to confirm the dependency edge.

The only fault-injection settings available to this run are switched off: every flag in otel-demo/flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off' and none targets Company.Ops or a database, so no injected-fault setting in the observed configuration explains the failures.

Rejected: that the cluster-wide in-place container restart at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z caused the job-creation 500s. The Company.Ops ERROR/WARN lines are at 05:28:09Z, 06:28:09Z and 07:28:09Z — before that restart — the restart kept the same pod names with the workloads Running and ready afterwards, and the Company.Ops hosts in the logs (ops-prod-01, ops-prod-02, radar-prod-01) are not pods of this cluster.

Pull the failover database's own logs and monitoring (deadlock/lock-wait, connection-pool saturation, timeout counters) for 2026-11-22T04:28Z–08:28Z; that dependency is not covered by any source available in this run, and its evidence is what would confirm or refute the failover-DB hypothesis.

Obtain the DR-test change record for correlation_id dr-test-001 (planned window, failover/switchback steps, database targets) from change management, since the change_history integration is not available here, and confirm the jobs table has no leftover lock or partial row for correlation_id job-8831 before retrying the user's job creation.

gaps: The exact entity named 'companyopswebjob' was not found: the index's 12 documents carry only service values Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, and no Deployment/Pod/Service of that name exists in the queried cluster. Which real service the name refers to (the job-scheduler lines under Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob) is my interpretation, not established evidence.

The change_history integration is not available, so the DR-test change record (who ran dr-test-001, its scope, and when the failover was applied) could not be verified; the failover database is only referred to as 'failover DB'/'failover database'/'primary database' and has no name, logs or metrics in any authorized source.

All Prometheus calls failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query), so error-rate and latency readings for Company.Ops and for the database are unknown rather than zero; no baseline exists for a latency comparison.
Jaeger traces_list_services also failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the failed job-creation request could not be confirmed in traces and no span-level call edge to a database was observable.

The index is sparse (12 documents at one-per-hour boundaries, none between 04:28:09Z and 05:28:09Z), so the exact onset of the failures between those samples is unknown; the document count is the index state at query time, not during the incident.

The only in-window log line about creating a new scheduled job is correlation_id job-8831; no user identity or request ID is present, so the individual user's request cannot be matched to a log entry beyond that correlation id, and the reported '500s' plural is only singly attested for job creation (the other job-creation line records 503).

Name-match queries for CronJobs and Services returned nothing (no_data views, not usable as fact), so absence of such objects is unestablished; there are no CronJobs, and the 29 services included none whose name matched compan/ops/webjob/radar/app-254.

No Node events are present in the window (only the two Endpoints warnings), so the cause of the cluster-wide container restarts at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (presumably a node/container-runtime restart) is unknown and is recorded as a change during the window with an unidentified trigger, unrelated to the Company.Ops errors.
Impact downstream of Company.Ops/Rader (e.g. end users or other callers) was not observed; confirming it would require request-level traces or client-side error data that were not available.
